One of the things as a farmer, I just find very, very concerning knowing that we have a lot of hungry people in this country and coming to find out that fully 40% of the food that's produced in our country is wasted. Our legislation that I'm happy to co-sponsor with Ms. Pingree from the State of Maine is an effort to bring some clarity, I guess, and the confusion on what those dates on food products actually mean. Right now, there's no standardized definition for any of these dates. So best if used by freshness by all of these different things are just dates that are put on by individual companies to try to help consumers make decisions. And so I'm very happy to be able to work and a bipartisan way to address this issue. I'm the co-chairman of the food recovery caucus, and we'll continue to work on this so that we can try to reduce the amount of food that so many resources go into the protection, whether it's land and water, all of the inputs and labor that goes into the protection of food, and then we end up tossing so much of it out. truly egregious amount of waste and time inputs and money. Yeah, why the world would we be wanting to turn our backs on a source of energy that has allowed us to reduce our carbon footprint as dramatically as we have over the last couple of decades. It escapes me why that makes sense to anybody. But it's absolutely true. Sometimes things get arguments are made and debates get a little bit out of hand and accusations can fly. This is not an issue that has just been cooked up to get the political base excited so that we are in a better place for the next election. This is a true issue. We have evidence proof that this administration has been working on regulations to reduce the use of natural gas through kitchen appliances. This has been going on for over a year, in fact, and it's not just at the federal level. There are states in the country, New York, California, even my own state of Washington. There are regulations being promulgated to preclude natural gas from being used in new resident construction. And so my take on this, Jeff, just so you know, my eyes are wide open as to why this is happening. And I've got to say that this is kind of like the proverbial camel's nose under the edge of the tent scenario. This is an effort, and I think not a very well-covered effort to wean this country off of the use of fossil fuels as quickly as possible. And by removing consumer choice, by taking away one of the most efficient clean energy resources that we have for for reasons to move to renewable energy sources versus fossil fuels when natural gas and propane have such a tremendous track record of not only providing affordable clean energy source but is an abundance and allows millions of Americans. In fact, I think the number is something like 187 million Americans utilize gas for preparing their meals. This is just beyond the pale as to why this makes any sense at all. And so this is not an invented issue. This is something that we've been able to address here in Congress. We just passed a bill yesterday to preclude the Department of Energy from moving forward. with further regulations on this issue. And I hope the Senate takes it up and we can send it to the President for an accident into law. As proposed, the Department of Energy would cause at least half. And some people are saying over 90% of the gas stoves on the market today would fail. The regulatory tests that are being proposed by the Department of Energy essentially making it unattainable for millions of Americans to choose that resource choice, make that resource choice. In many parts of the country, we're blessed in the state of Washington, I think, for a lot of reasons. But we don't have hurricanes. We don't have tornadoes. Typically, we don't have the kind of natural disasters that many parts of the country do. When those things happen, almost every single time the power goes out. Most of the time you still have your gas supply available to you, so people in an emergency situation can still utilize gas to prepare their meals. So, there's so many reasons why this is an important issue.
